children.text: Sagbayan Peak is a hilltop park in San Agustin, Bohol, that is reported closed. It was still closed in an April 2025 report, and a local operator checked in November 2026 routes tours to the Chocolate Hills viewpoint in Carmen. Plan around Carmen until an official reopening is confirmed.

Sagbayan Peak is a hilltop park in San Agustin, Sagbayan, in north-central Bohol. Visitors once looked over the valley and limestone hills from its ridge deck. The Carmen Chocolate Hills viewpoint is a separate site.
Sagbayan is a rural municipality of about 25,000 people with an area of about
70 km²
, at an elevation of about

according to Wikipedia. It was created in 1949 under the name Borja and renamed Sagbayan in 1957, and because it was near the epicenter of the magnitude 7.2 Bohol earthquake in 2013, its town hall was destroyed. Because it is a rural area with few tourism facilities, it helps to know that a park like this provides a few local jobs.
According to the
Philippine Daily Inquirer’s April 2025 reporting

listed Sagbayan Peak in San Agustin and Captain’s Peak in Canmano as still closed at the time. Captain’s Peak closed on 14 March 2024 after the Sagbayan municipality revoked its business permit, but the exact closure date and reason for Sagbayan Peak could not be confirmed from sources. Historic prices and hours should be left out of current plans.

The Carmen viewpoint is a main place to see the Chocolate Hills, with numerous limestone mounds in view at once. Check the separate names and addresses of Sagbayan Peak, Captain’s Peak, and the Carmen viewpoint on maps and tour itineraries.
When the park was open, the deck overlooked limestone hills and valleys. Access now depends on a reopening notice.
A
local tour operator
routes visitors to the Carmen viewpoint during the Sagbayan Peak closure. Confirm your actual stop before booking.
This was one of the park’s facilities. Ask the Sagbayan tourism desk about access and prices after reopening.
The park housed a tarsier exhibit when open. For a current Bohol visit, check the opening days of the sanctuary in Corella.
The café and covered rest area predate the closure. Plan food stops in Carmen or Loboc.
Dinosaur and cartoon sculptures were among the park’s attractions. Access depends on a reopening notice.
Chocolate Hills Adventure Park
is a separate facility in Carmen. It offers a bike zipline and other activities, with a separate ticket from the viewpoint.
Bohol’s
provincial tourism office
lists the Sagbayan tourism desk at +63 920 775 0869. Ask about reopening and available facilities before traveling.

To add Sagbayan Peak, first confirm the municipality’s reopening date and last admission time.

items.title: Inland Bohol in one day
items.subtitle: Views and nature in one trip

children.text: Set out on a car tour from Panglao or Tagbilaran. Have a light breakfast and bring water.
Visit the tarsier sanctuary in Corella after confirming its hours for that date.
See the ridge and limestone mounds at the Carmen Chocolate Hills viewpoint.
Head toward the Loboc River and have lunch.
Choose an accessible stop such as the Bilar Man-Made Forest or an activity in Carmen.
Return to your lodging before sunset.
If a tour advertises both the Carmen viewpoint and Sagbayan Peak, ask the operator where it will stop on your travel date.
Take a domestic flight from Manila Ninoy Aquino International Airport to Bohol–Panglao International Airport (TAG).
From Cebu, another option is the ferry to Tagbilaran.

items.title: By car from Tagbilaran or Panglao

children.text: When booking a car and driver from Panglao or Tagbilaran, specify the Carmen viewpoint or the adventure park as your drop-off.
Tours listing Sagbayan Peak may divert to Carmen during the closure. Check the itinerary and terms.
If Sagbayan Peak reopens, confirm the San Agustin entrance and your return ride before setting off.
At Tagbilaran’s Dao terminal, ask about services and drop-offs toward Carmen or Sagbayan.
The Carmen viewpoint and Sagbayan Peak have different stops. Confirm the destination and return ride.
For a clear view in Carmen, aim for a morning with a low chance of rain in
December–May
From
June–November
, rain and clouds often block the view, and after a typhoon the roads can be in poor shape. Check the forecast before you go.
Use the weather table below for the Carmen alternatives. Sagbayan Peak visiting dates depend on an official reopening notice.

children.text: Carmen activities and transport prices are operator listings checked in
November 2026
. Look for Sagbayan Peak admission details in the reopening notice.
The park had a café and pavilion before it closed. Allow time for a meal in Carmen or Loboc on a current itinerary.

There are not many restaurants around the park, so it is easier to have lunch in Carmen, where the Chocolate Hills are, or on the Loboc side. Many people use Alona Beach on Panglao Island or Tagbilaran as their base. The Loboc River cruise lunch is well known as a lunch stop on tours, but the travel time is long, so avoid packing too many places into one day. If you leave early in the morning, you can also eat a light breakfast at your Tagbilaran or Panglao lodging before you go.
Choose a clear morning for the Carmen viewpoint.

Sagbayan Peak in San Agustin and Captain’s Peak in Canmano are separate sites. Give the attraction and barangay names when consulting the operator or tourism desk.
